meta.title: Zoho Books (India edition) import rules
meta.purpose: Rules for checking every file before it is imported into Zoho Books, and for explaining an error file Zoho gives back. Companion document: docs/ZOHO_IMPORT_RULES.md.

evidence_levels.confirmed by our import: Seen in a test import (real-data/zoho-import-1, real-data/zoho-test-2): the file was accepted or refused in this way.
evidence_levels.Zoho documentation: Said on a Zoho help, FAQ or API page; source_url gives the page.
evidence_levels.Zoho sample file: Taken from Zoho's own sample import file in zoho-samples/ (its example rows or its Field Explanation sheet).
evidence_levels.forum: Reported by a user on a forum; source_url gives the thread. Not confirmed by Zoho.
evidence_levels.assumed: A reasoned guess. Not confirmed anywhere. Listed so that the next test import can settle it.
evidence_levels.Contradicted by second import: The second test import (real-data/zoho-test-2) showed that Zoho does NOT refuse this. The rule is kept as a warning only and is counted as not confirmed.
evidence_levels.Read from live organisations: Read from two new India organisations of Zoho Books (created 2026-11-14) with Zoho's own lists, read only: what Zoho Books itself holds. Counted like "confirmed by our import".
evidence_levels.Confirmed by second import: Seen in the second test import (real-data/zoho-test-2): Zoho accepted or refused the file in this way. Counted like "confirmed by our import".

severities.blocks_import: Zoho refuses the row or the file. The tool should not let the file be downloaded as ready.
severities.warning: Zoho may accept the row but the result may be wrong, or the rule is not yet confirmed. Show it; let the user decide.

kinds.required: The column must have a value on every row. params.target = "mapping" or "organisation_setting" means the rule is about the import screen or a setting, not a cell.
kinds.enum: The value must be one of params.values, or one of the entries of the list named in params.list (field params.field). params.allowEmpty, params.caseSensitive.
kinds.regex: The value must match params.pattern (JavaScript syntax). params.allowEmpty.
kinds.maxLength: At most params.max characters. With params.concat, the joined length of those columns.
kinds.unique: params.scope "file": no two rows with the same value. "document": rows with the same params.groupBy are one document; params.headerColumnsMustMatch must be equal on all of them. "across_files": the value must not be in the other files named.
kinds.reference: The value must exist in params.target ("<module>.<column>" of another file of the same job, or "zoho.<thing>" = something that exists in the Zoho Books organisation) or in params.orIn. Matching is exact unless said.
kinds.conditional: params.when (column, op, value) decides the rows; params.then is what must hold. Or params.check names a check on the whole row, document, file or organisation. params.watchList (on a warning): a row like it was refused once for a reason that is not known; the row is not blocked, and rows of other files that name it carry the same warning.
kinds.forbidden: The value must NOT be one of params.values / the list; or the columns in params.mustBeEmpty must be empty when params.when holds; or (params.target "headings") the column must not be in the file.

param_checks.information: Nothing to check; a fact the user should know.
param_checks.flag: Show the row to the user.
param_checks.process: About the order or way of working, not about a cell.
param_checks.organisation_setting: Depends on a setting in Zoho Books named in params.setting.
param_checks.all_or_none: The columns are all filled or all empty.
param_checks.at_least_one: At least one of params.anyOf holds.
param_checks.at_most_one: At most one of the columns is filled.
param_checks.exactly_one_positive: Exactly one of the columns has an amount above zero.
param_checks.group_sum_equal: Within each group of params.groupBy, the sums of params.left and params.right are equal.
param_checks.group_min_rows: Each group has at least params.min rows.
param_checks.group_sum_max: Within each group the sum of params.sum is not above params.maxColumn.
param_checks.document_sum_min: The document total is at least params.min.
param_checks.intra_inter_state: Compares the state column with the organisation state (or the other state column) and checks the tax prefix and tax type. With params.emptyStateMeans "same_for_unregistered" an empty first state on a row whose GST Treatment is business_none or consumer counts as the same state as the other.
param_checks.gstin_prefix_matches_state: The first two digits of the GSTIN equal gstin_prefix of the state code.
param_checks.reference_or_empty: Empty, or something that exists in Zoho Books.
param_checks.arrived_in_zoho: A record of a master file that the export of Zoho Books, taken after the import and given in the Import Wizard, does not have. Checked only when that export was given.
param_checks.reference_written_as_master: A name of a later file that is in the master file only once spaces and line breaks at its ends are left out. Applied by every reference rule.
param_checks.equals_setting: Equals a setting of the organisation.
param_checks.date_on_or_before_setting: The date is on or before a date setting.
param_checks.tds_name_not_zoho_default: A TDS Name that is also the name of a TDS tax Zoho has (its export, or Zoho's default taxes) must match that tax's rate and section.
param_checks.required_when_setting: The column must hold at least params.minDigits digits when the organisation setting params.setting (from the Import Wizard answers) is on; skipped when the setting is off or unknown.
param_checks.opening_date_confirmed: For a contacts file with opening balances: a step to do first, until the date Zoho Books shows on Settings > Opening Balances was typed in the Import Wizard (step "Save the Migration Date") and equals the Migration Date of the tool. The rows are not refused; the file is not "ready" until then.
param_checks.account_type_in: A journal line whose Account is an account of the Chart of Accounts file with an Account Type in params.types.

file_format.encoding: UTF-8 (Unicode), the default of the import page

column_classes.note: The general format rules name a class of columns (params.target), not a column. These are the classes. A column that has a format rule of its own in its module is left to that rule.

while_importing.note: What to know while importing. The Import Wizard shows the entries whose modules include a file on that file's step (null: every file); READ_ME_FIRST.txt and READ_ME_IMPORT_ORDER.txt print every entry. docs/ZOHO_IMPORT_RULES.md, section "While you import", has the same texts.

entries.text: Import one file at a time, in the order of the Import Wizard. Wait until Zoho Books says an import has finished before you start the next.

The "ready" figure of Zoho's preview is not proof. In the third test import the preview said every customer was ready, and Zoho Books created one fewer without saying so. After the import, export the list from Zoho Books and upload it in the Import Wizard: the tool names every record that is missing.
entries.seen: third test import: Customers (one customer of the file was not created)

entries.text: A journal refused with "Invalid row" on its Accounts Receivable or Accounts Payable line, and "This error is related to Row N - Contact Name." on its other lines, names a customer or vendor that is not in Zoho Books. That was the only refusal of the third test import: a receipt journal whose customer had not been created. Import the missing customer or vendor first, then the refused journal again.
entries.seen: third test import: one receipt journal of the receipts, payments and contra file

entries.text: A journal with a customer or vendor on Accounts Receivable or Accounts Payable (Contact Name filled) and a bank or cash line in the same journal is accepted by Zoho Books: such journals were accepted in the third test import. Do not split or change them. Each one leaves a credit on the contact, which the page "Apply the credits" applies to the invoice or bill it pays.
entries.seen: third test import: ten such journals were accepted, and the refused one was accepted in an organisation that had its customer

entries.text: If Zoho Books shows "Nothing handled the action gotoImportPreview" on its own page (not in an error file), the file is not the problem. Reload the page in the browser and start that import again from Choose File.
entries.seen: third test import: once, on the Vendors import; reloading the page solved it (zoho-screens, screen 52)

entries.text: If Zoho Books refuses rows, download its error file and give it to the tool (the step of that file, or the Rejection Manager). It says in plain words why each row was refused and gives a file with only the rows to import again.

wizard_steps: Character Encoding and File Delimiter (and the module's own options)
Map Fields: check each field, set date format, do not map total columns
Preview: read the count of rows ready and rows with errors

rules.message: Zoho imports only CSV, TSV and XLS files.
rules.fix: Write a CSV file in UTF-8 with a comma between values, and leave Character Encoding at UTF-8 (Unicode) on the import page.

rules.message: The file is larger than Zoho accepts for this module.
rules.fix: Split the file into parts, keeping every line of one document in the same part.

rules.message: A file with more than 151 columns is refused.
rules.fix: Remove unused columns.

rules.message: A column without a heading stops the import.
rules.fix: Do not write an empty column or a comma after the last heading.

rules.message: A row with more or fewer values than headings shifts the columns.
rules.fix: Quote every value that contains a comma, a quote or a line break.

rules.message: A value contains a hidden character or a line break inside it. Two names that look the same would then not match.
rules.fix: Look at the value in Mapping Studio > Names. The tool writes a name exactly as in Tally, the same way in every file; clean it there only if Zoho Books refuses it.
rules.evidence_note: Spaces or a line break at the START or END of a customer or vendor name, and a line break INSIDE it, are NOT counted here: in the third test import 32 names that end in spaces and a line break and 1 name with a line break inside it were accepted, and read back from the organisation Zoho Books keeps each name exactly as written (with the line break). They are a warning only (GEN-NO-OUTER-SPACES). Any other hidden character, or a line break in another column, has not been tried.

rules.message: Zoho advises removing apostrophes and asterisks from import files.
rules.fix: Check these names in the Preview step. In our import names with % & ( ) - . : @ and one name with an apostrophe were accepted; an asterisk has not been tried.
rules.evidence_note: First test import: one vendor Display Name with an apostrophe was imported. No name with an asterisk was in the files.

rules.message: A name starts or ends with a space or a line break, or has a line break inside it. Zoho Books keeps the name exactly as written, so every later file must write it the same way.
rules.fix: Nothing to do for a customer or vendor name: the tool writes it exactly as in Tally, the same way in every file, and compares it with Zoho's exports without the spaces and line breaks. For another name, check it in the Preview step.
rules.evidence_note: Third test import: 32 customer and vendor names that end in spaces and a line break, and 1 with a line break inside it, were accepted. Read back from the organisation (read only), Zoho Books keeps them exactly as written, line break included. None of them was named in a voucher file, so a later file naming such a contact has not been tried; the tool writes the same name in every file.

rules.message: Dates are written yyyy-MM-dd (for example 2025-04-01), and each must be a real calendar day (2025-09-31 or 2026-02-29 does not exist and is refused).
rules.fix: On the Map Fields page choose the date format yyyy-MM-dd for each date field (Zoho's default is "Select format at field level").
rules.evidence_note: yyyy-MM-dd was accepted in our Manual Journals import (39 journals). The list of formats is in the invoice and journal sample files.

rules.message: Amounts are plain numbers with a dot and at most two decimals: no commas, no currency sign, no Dr/Cr.
rules.fix: Write 1234567.89. Leave Decimal Format at 1234567.89 on the Map Fields page.

rules.message: A percentage is a number without the % sign.
rules.fix: Write 18, not 18%.

rules.message: A name that points to something in Zoho Books (account, customer, vendor, item, tax) must be written exactly as it is there: same spelling, spaces and capital letters.
rules.fix: Take names from one place only (the file the tool creates, or an export from Zoho Books).

rules.message: Every field Zoho marks with a red asterisk on the Map Fields page must be mapped to a column.
rules.fix: Check the Map Fields page before pressing Next.

rules.message: Zoho runs one import at a time.
rules.fix: Wait until the earlier import has finished before starting the next file.

rules.message: The Import option is shown only to a user who may view and create that kind of transaction.
rules.fix: Use an admin user, or give the role View and Create rights (Settings > Users & Roles > Roles).

params.row_numbering: heading row is row 1, first data row is row 2

rules.message: In Zoho's error file ROWNUMBER counts the heading as row 1.
rules.fix: Subtract 1 to get the data row.

rules.message: When one line of an invoice, bill or journal is wrong, every line of that document is refused: the wrong line carries the message, the others say "This error is related to Row N - <column>."
rules.fix: Correct the line named and import the whole document again.

rules.message: The name is in the master file (Chart of Accounts, Customers, Vendors or Items), but written there with other spaces or line breaks at its start or end. Zoho matches names exactly, so the two files must write the name the same way.
rules.fix: Create the files again: the tool writes a name the same way in every file. If the file was changed by hand, write the name exactly as in the master file.
rules.evidence_note: Not seen in an import: the files the tool creates always write a name the same way, so this fires only on a file changed by hand. Read back after the third import, Zoho Books keeps a contact name exactly as written (a line break at its end included), so whether Zoho matches the same name written with other spaces at its ends is not known; it is marked "may be refused" until an import shows it.

rules.message: This record is in the file but not in Zoho Books: the export of Zoho Books given in the Import Wizard does not have it. Zoho Books did not create it, although the file was imported. Every later file that names it would be refused.
rules.fix: Import Wizard, step of this file: download the file with only the missing rows and import it (after the Migration Date is saved, so an opening balance gets the right date). Then export from Zoho Books again and upload the new export.
rules.evidence_note: Third test import: the preview of the Customers import said every row was ready, and Zoho Books then created one customer fewer than the file had. No error file was given. The opening balance of that customer was missing from Accounts Receivable, and the journal that named it was refused later. The check runs only when Zoho's own export of the file (taken after the import) was given in the Import Wizard; names are compared without spaces around them, with runs of spaces and line breaks as one space, and without capital letters (Zoho Books keeps a name exactly as imported, but an export opened and saved in a spreadsheet may lose the spaces and line breaks at its ends).

organisation_setup.do: It is the Settings (gear) icon at the top right of Zoho Books; the Settings page has the columns Organization, Users & Roles, Setup & Configurations, Customization and Automation, and a group Taxes & Compliance with Taxes, Direct Taxes and e-Way Bills. Check the organisation name and address. The state of the organisation must be the state of the GSTIN. Base Currency: INR. Fiscal Year: the months of the financial year of the Tally company, shown below for this migration. The date format can be any you like, because each import screen asks for the date format of its file.

organisation_setup.where: Settings > Taxes & Compliance > Taxes > GST Settings
organisation_setup.do: Choose that the business is registered for GST (Is your business registered for GST? Yes). Enter the GSTIN and the GST registration date. Choose Regular, or Composition Scheme if the business is under it. Tick Reverse Charge only if the business pays GST under reverse charge; the tool says below whether its bills need it. Tick SEZ / Overseas Trading only if the business buys from or sells to parties outside India or in an SEZ; the tool says below whether its parties need it. If you tick SEZ / Overseas Trading, Zoho Books makes the Custom Duty Tracking Account a required field: choose any expense account, because this migration does not use it. Zoho then creates the default tax rates and the GST accounts.

organisation_setup.where: Settings > Taxes & Compliance > Direct Taxes > Income TDS Settings; Settings > Taxes & Compliance > Direct Taxes > Income TDS Rates
organisation_setup.do: Open Income TDS Settings and check that TDS is switched on for the organisation. Open Income TDS Rates and look at the TDS taxes Zoho Books already has. Click + New TDS Tax for each tax in the list "TDS taxes to create" below, with exactly that name, rate and section code (the names are the ones chosen in the tool, in Mapping Studio, TDS mapping). Zoho Books asks for the Applicable Income Tax Act first: choose the Old Income Tax Act 1961 when the migration has transactions before 01/04/2026 (Zoho Books shows the New Income Tax Act 2025 by default). Set the start date of every tax on or before the first day of the financial year. Fill the rate and the section code of every tax. A tax that shows Expired is fine for past years. Do not use a name Zoho Books already has for another rate or section (it has its own Commission or Brokerage); the list uses unique names. rules.evidence_note: The API says the purchase account is mandatory for purchase, sales-and-purchase and inventory items. Our 29 rows had it empty and would have failed on this next.

rules.message: An item that can be purchased needs a Purchase Rate (cost price).
rules.fix: Enter the purchase rate in Mapping Studio > Rates, or change Item Type to Sales.

rules.message: An Inventory item needs an Inventory Account, and inventory tracking must be turned on in Zoho Books.
rules.fix: Write the stock account, or use "Sales and Purchases" when stock is not tracked in Zoho.

rules.message: An HSN or SAC code has 4, 6 or 8 digits and nothing else. A 5-digit code was refused in our Invoices import.
rules.fix: Write a code of at least 6 digits (a service uses the 6-digit SAC, which starts with 99). Choose a default code for the income ledger or service item in Mapping Studio (HSN/SAC), or switch the HSN/SAC field off in Zoho Books (Settings, Setup and Configurations, Items) and say so in the Import Wizard.
rules.evidence_note: Refusal of 5 digits is confirmed (Invoices file). That 4, 6 and 8 are the accepted lengths is assumed: Zoho's setting offers 4-digit or 6-digit, the column allows 8.

rules.message: A service takes a SAC, which starts with 99. An HSN code on a service is refused later by the e-invoice portal.
rules.fix: Use the SAC of the service.

rules.message: The tax names must exist in Zoho Books: a GST tax group for Intra State (GST18), an IGST tax for Inter State (IGST18).
rules.fix: Use the default names or create the tax first in Settings > Taxes & Compliance > Taxes > Tax Rates.

rules.message: The intra-state tax type is "Group".
rules.fix: Write Group.

rules.message: The inter-state tax type is "Simple".
rules.fix: Write Simple.

rules.message: A taxable item has both an intra-state and an inter-state tax, at the same rate.
rules.fix: Fill both or neither.

rules.message: Taxability Type is empty (taxable), Out Of Scope or Non-GST Supply. A non-taxable item carries an Exemption Reason instead.
rules.fix: Use the spelling of the sample file ("Out Of Scope" with a capital O in Of).
rules.evidence_note: "Out Of Scope" and "Non-GST Supply" are in the sample; "Taxable" and "Non-Taxable" are assumed.

rules.message: An Exemption Reason must exist in Settings > Taxes & Compliance > Taxes > Tax Exemptions.
rules.fix: Create the exemption first, with exactly this name.

rules.message: Status is Active or Inactive.
rules.fix: Write Active.

rules.message: An SKU must be unique.
rules.fix: Leave empty or give each item its own SKU.

rules.message: At most 2000 characters.
rules.fix: Shorten.

rules.message: The column "CF.custom_field" of the sample belongs to Zoho's demo organisation.
rules.fix: Leave the column out.

invoices.label: Invoices
click_path: Link Invoices to its corresponding Sales Orders: NOT ticked
Map the customers' addresses ...: NOT ticked
Map Fields (Date format yyyy-MM-dd, Decimal format 1234567.89)

auto_generate_invoice_numbers.why: when ticked, the invoice numbers of the file are ignored

map_customer_addresses.why: when ticked, a customer that is not found is created as a new customer, so a misspelt name does not show as an error

invoices.one_row_is: one line of an invoice; the invoice's own fields are repeated on every line
must_exist_first: Items (if Item Name is an item of the Items file)
TDS taxes (if TDS Name is written)
Settings > Setup & Configurations > General: Adjustments on, Rounding off in Sales Transactions = No Rounding

rules.message: Every row needs the Invoice Number.
rules.fix: Write the Tally voucher number.

rules.message: An Invoice Number has at most 50 characters.
rules.fix: Shorten the number.

rules.message: Rows with the same Invoice Number are the lines of one invoice. Two different invoices must not share a number, and an invoice number already in Zoho Books is refused.
rules.fix: When Tally has the same number twice (for example in two series), add the series to the number.

rules.message: Zoho Books works the tax out from the rate on each line and ignores Tally's tax amount. For these invoices the tax at the rate written is not Tally's tax by more than rounding, so the invoice is imported but comes to another total than in Tally.
rules.fix: Correct the rate or the amount in Tally, or map the tax ledger to the Zoho tax of the right rate in Mapping Studio (Tax mapping), then create the files again. Or accept Zoho's figure and correct the invoice in Zoho Books after the import.

rules.message: Every row needs the Invoice Date.
rules.fix: Write the voucher date as yyyy-MM-dd.

rules.message: Every row needs the Customer Name.
rules.fix: Write the customer's Display Name.

rules.message: The customer must be in Zoho Books with exactly this Display Name.
rules.fix: Import the Customers file first; do not tick "Map the customers' addresses", or Zoho creates a new customer for every name it does not find.

rules.message: At most 100 characters.
rules.fix: Use the shortened name of the Customers file.

rules.message: Zoho marks Item Name as mandatory on every invoice line. This line has none.
rules.fix: The tool writes the Tally stock item of a stock item line; any other line carries the service item named after its account, which is added to the Items file (rate 0.00, Item Type Sales, that account). Import the Items file first.
rules.evidence_note: Not yet seen as an error, because every invoice failed first on the HSN code. First test import: Item Name was empty on every line; it did not show as an error only because the HSN check failed first.

rules.message: At most 200 characters.
rules.fix: Shorten.

rules.message: The Item Name of an invoice line should be an item in Zoho Books with exactly this name. Whether Zoho refuses an unknown name or creates the item is not confirmed.
rules.fix: Import the Items file first: it holds the stock items and the service items the invoices use.

rules.message: At most 2000 characters.
rules.fix: Shorten.

rules.message: Every line needs an Item Price.
rules.fix: Write the rate of the line.

rules.message: A line with a negative price. Zoho may refuse it: not confirmed. TDS deducted by the customer and round-off are not written as lines (they go to the TDS columns and to Adjustment).
rules.fix: Choose the Zoho TDS tax for a TDS ledger in Mapping Studio (TDS mapping); for a discount, an accountant decides (Discount, a credit note or a journal).
rules.evidence_note: First test import: the negative lines were TDS deducted by the customer and round-off.

rules.message: The Account of a line must be an income account that exists in Zoho Books with exactly this name.
rules.fix: Import the Chart of Accounts first.

rules.message: A tax, TDS or receivable account should not be an invoice line. Zoho posts GST from the Item Tax columns and TDS from the TDS columns. Whether Zoho refuses such a line is not known.
rules.fix: Move GST ledgers to Item Tax, TDS to the TDS columns.
rules.evidence_note: First test import: the file had lines on TDS Receivable.

rules.message: An HSN or SAC code has only digits and at least 6 of them when the HSN/SAC field is switched on in Zoho Books. A 5-digit code was refused in our imports.
rules.fix: Write a code of at least 6 digits (a service uses the 6-digit SAC, which starts with 99). Choose a default code for the income ledger or service item in Mapping Studio (HSN/SAC), or switch the HSN/SAC field off in Zoho Books (Settings, Setup and Configurations, Items) and say so in the Import Wizard.
rules.evidence_note: 28 invoices refused for a 5-digit code. The accepted lengths (4, 6, 8) are assumed.

rules.message: GST Treatment must be one of Zoho's codes.
rules.fix: Write the same code as on the customer.

rules.message: A registered customer needs a valid GSTIN on the invoice.
rules.fix: Correct it in Fix contacts.

rules.message: No GSTIN for an unregistered, consumer or overseas customer.
rules.fix: Remove it or change the treatment.

rules.message: Place of Supply is a two-letter state code from Zoho's list.
rules.fix: Use the code from the list.

rules.message: An invoice to a party in India needs a Place of Supply; it decides between GST and IGST. If empty Zoho takes the customer's Place Of Contact.
rules.fix: Write the state of the customer.

rules.message: An export invoice has no Indian state.
rules.fix: Leave empty.

rules.message: Each line must say how it stands for GST: a tax, an exemption reason, or a supply type Non-GST Supply or Out of Scope. This line has none of these.
rules.fix: Taxable: Item Tax, Item Tax Type and Item Tax %. Exempt: Item Tax Exemption Reason (and Supply Type Exempted). Outside GST: Supply Type Out of Scope or Non-GST Supply. Export: IGST0.
rules.evidence_note: Zoho documents the error "specify whether it is tax or not". Not yet seen in our import because the HSN error came first. First test import: no line had any of these; the invoices failed earlier on the HSN check.

rules.message: The Item Tax name must exist in Zoho Books (GST18, IGST18 ...). A name Zoho does not know may be created as a new tax.
rules.fix: Use the names from Mapping Studio > Tax mapping.

rules.message: Item Tax Type is ItemAmount (for IGST) or Tax Group (for GST).
rules.fix: Write it as in the sample file, without a space in ItemAmount.

rules.message: Item Tax, Item Tax Type and Item Tax % go together.
rules.fix: Fill all three or none.

rules.message: Same state as the organisation: a GST tax group (type Tax Group). Another state, or export: an IGST tax (type ItemAmount).
rules.fix: Correct the tax or the Place of Supply.

rules.message: The line carries one of Zoho's taxes named for its rate (GST18, IGST5 ...) with another percentage. A Zoho tax has one rate: Zoho Books works the tax out at the rate of the tax named, so the line's tax and the invoice total would differ from Tally, or the line is refused.
rules.fix: Write Zoho's tax of the line's rate (leave the Tally ledger unmapped in Mapping Studio, Tax mapping, so each line gets the tax of its own rate) and create the files again.
rules.evidence_note: Audit item GST-001: no import has shown what Zoho does with a tax name whose rate differs from Item Tax %.

rules.message: Supply Type is Taxable, Exempted, Non-GST Supply or Out of Scope.
rules.fix: Use the spelling of the invoice sample ("Out of Scope", small o).

rules.message: An exemption reason must exist in Settings > Taxes & Compliance > Taxes > Tax Exemptions.
rules.fix: Create it first with exactly this name.

rules.message: At most 50 characters.
rules.fix: Shorten.

rules.message: A taxed invoice line of a customer in India with no Place of Supply. Zoho Books then takes the customer's Place Of Contact; for a customer with none it is believed to take the organisation's own state, which would make an inter-state invoice (IGST) an intra-state one and refuse or change its tax. Not confirmed by an import.
rules.fix: Give the customer's state in Tally (or the customer's GSTIN) and create the files again.
rules.evidence_note: Audit item GST-024 (A12). Test 2 confirmed only IGST0 on overseas invoices with an empty Place of Supply.

params.noneWords: No invoice has a TDS Amount that differs from its TDS Percentage of the base by more than a rupee.

rules.message: The TDS Amount of these invoices (Tally's) is not the TDS Percentage of the base by more than a rupee. Whether Zoho Books keeps the amount as written, works it out again from the percentage, or refuses the invoice when they differ has not been seen in an import.
rules.fix: Import one such invoice first and compare its TDS with Tally. If Zoho works it out again, set the right percentage in Mapping Studio (TDS mapping) and create the files again.
rules.evidence_note: Audit item TDS-005.

rules.message: A TDS Name must be a TDS tax in Zoho Books.
rules.fix: Pick the Zoho TDS tax in Mapping Studio (TDS mapping). With no choice the tool writes the one suggested from the section in Tally; check that it exists in Settings > Taxes & Compliance > Direct Taxes > Income TDS Rates.
rules.evidence_note: Third test import: every bill and invoice row with a TDS Name was accepted after the TDS taxes were created in Zoho Books with exactly the names, rates and section codes the tool lists ("TDS taxes to create"). The tool cannot see the TDS taxes of the organisation, so these rows stay "may be refused" until the TDS export of Zoho Books is given in the Import Wizard (step "Set up Zoho Books"); with the export every name is checked.

rules.message: A TDS Amount needs the TDS Name it belongs to.
rules.fix: Map the Tally TDS ledger to a Zoho TDS tax in Mapping Studio > TDS mapping.

rules.message: Enter the required TDS details. TDS Name, TDS Percentage and TDS Section Code are all filled on a row with TDS, or all empty.
rules.fix: Write the percentage and the section code on every invoice row that has a TDS Name. The tool works the percentage out from Tally's TDS amount and takes the section code from the TDS table (see TDS mapping and the Assumptions list).
rules.evidence_note: Second test import (real-data/zoho-test-2): Zoho refused every row that had TDS Name and TDS Amount but empty TDS Percentage and TDS Section Code with "Enter the required TDS details." (bills: 101 rows, invoices: 2).

rules.message: TDS Section Code must be a section of the Income Tax Act, 1961 (for example 194J) or a code of Zoho's list for the Income Tax Act, 2025 (for example professional_fees). A code in neither will be refused. A form of the other act than the document's date (an old section number on a document from 1 April 2026, or a new code before it) may be refused.
rules.fix: Choose a known section in Mapping Studio (TDS mapping), or set the tax act in Voucher files.
rules.evidence_note: TDS-018. Zoho lists the codes the TDS Section Code column takes (lists.tds.section_codes_income_tax_act_2025); its own export of the second test import gives 194J / 194H for taxes of the old act. A text in neither list is refused (will). Whether a form of the other act is accepted for a date has not been tried: may be refused (tier 2 variant 'act').

rules.message: This TDS Name is also the name of a TDS tax Zoho Books already has, with another rate or section. Two taxes with one name are easy to mix up.
rules.fix: Use a name that Zoho does not already use for another rate (the tool adds the section and rate to the name), or use the tax Zoho has.
rules.evidence_note: In the second test import Zoho already had "Commission or Brokerage" at 2% (new act) and our tax of the same name was 5% (old act). Not refused, but unsafe.

rules.message: Adjustment is a plus or minus amount added to the total, written once per invoice.
rules.fix: Put round-off here, with "Round Off" in Adjustment Description. Turn on Adjustments in Settings > Setup & Configurations > General.

rules.message: At most 100 characters.
rules.fix: Shorten.

rules.message: Discount Type is item_level or entity_level.
rules.fix: Leave empty when there is no discount.

rules.message: A discount percentage is between 0 and 100.
rules.fix: Use Discount Amount / Entity Discount Amount for a fixed amount.

rules.message: Invoice Status must be a status Zoho knows.
rules.fix: Write open (unpaid) or draft.
rules.evidence_note: "open" was written in our file; not refused.

rules.message: true or false.
rules.fix: Write false.

rules.message: Quantity is a positive number.
rules.fix: Write 1 for a line without a quantity.

rules.message: Item Type is goods or service.
rules.fix: Write service for a service line, so the code is read as a SAC.

rules.message: These columns point to things that must already exist in Zoho Books (estimate, project, template, salesperson, branch, warehouse). An estimate number that does not exist gives "Resource does not exist".
rules.fix: Leave them empty unless the thing exists.

rules.message: Three-letter currency code.
rules.fix: Write INR; for another currency also write the Exchange Rate.

rules.message: At most 5000 characters.
rules.fix: Shorten.

rules.message: A date inside a locked period is refused.
rules.fix: Unlock Sales in Accountant > Transaction Locking for the import.

rules.message: Please ensure that the length of the HSN code is a minimum of 6 digits and it has only numbers. Zoho refuses an invoice line with an empty or short HSN/SAC when the HSN/SAC field is switched on (it is on by default in a new India organisation).
rules.fix: Give the income ledger or service item an HSN/SAC code (Mapping Studio, HSN/SAC), or switch the field off in Zoho Books (Settings, Setup and Configurations, Items) and answer "No" to the HSN/SAC question in the Import Wizard.
rules.evidence_note: 26 invoices refused in test 2 for an empty or 5-digit code while the field was on.

bills.label: Bills
click_path: Link bills to its corresponding Purchase Orders: NOT ticked
Map Fields (leave Total, SubTotal and Balance unmapped)
bills.one_row_is: one line of a bill; the bill's own fields are repeated on every line
must_exist_first: TDS taxes (if TDS Name is written)
Reverse charge enabled, if reverse charge taxes are written
Settings > Setup & Configurations > General: Adjustments on

what_it_showed: Every line of a registered vendor (business_gst) without tax was refused for the missing tax (98 lines, 64 bills).
Every other line (business_none or empty treatment) was refused only for the empty Total column (189 lines, 102 bills).
The total Zoho worked out was the plain sum of the line Rates, negative lines included, in all 102 bills.

rules.message: Every row needs the Bill Number.
rules.fix: Write the supplier invoice number; if Tally has none, the voucher number.

rules.message: Rows with the same Bill Number and vendor are the lines of one bill. The API says a bill number must be unique in the organisation; two vendors with the same bill number may therefore clash.
rules.fix: When two vendors use the same number, check the first import of such a pair; if refused, add a short vendor mark to the number.
rules.evidence_note: Third test import: bills of different vendors that share one Bill Number were all accepted (each is its own bill; Zoho Books keeps bill numbers per vendor). The check shows them as a warning only.

rules.message: Zoho Books works the tax out from the rate on each line and ignores Tally's tax amount. For these bills the tax at the rate written is not Tally's tax by more than rounding, so the bill is imported but comes to another total than in Tally.
rules.fix: Correct the rate or the amount in Tally, or map the tax ledger to the Zoho tax of the right rate in Mapping Studio (Tax mapping), then create the files again. Or accept Zoho's figure and correct the bill in Zoho Books after the import.

rules.message: Every row needs the Bill Date.
rules.fix: Write the voucher date as yyyy-MM-dd.

rules.message: Every row needs the Vendor Name.
rules.fix: Write the vendor's Display Name.

rules.message: The vendor must be in Zoho Books with exactly this Display Name.
rules.fix: Import the Vendors file first.

rules.message: A bill line without an item needs the expense Account.
rules.fix: Write the ledger of the line.

rules.message: The Account must exist in Zoho Books with exactly this name.
rules.fix: Import the Chart of Accounts first.

rules.message: A bill line posts to an account of a kind no import has shown on a bill line (equity, a non-current or other liability, a credit card, Accounts Payable or an output tax account). Zoho Books may refuse the bill, and if it does the vendor, the tax and this account all differ from Tally.
rules.fix: Import one such bill first and look at the result. If Zoho refuses it, route the Tally voucher as a Manual Journal in Voucher Classification and create the files again.
rules.evidence_note: Round 1 of the re-check. Expense, cost of goods sold and asset lines are the bills of every test import; Other Current Liability lines (a professional tax ledger) were in the round-3 import, in which all 157 bills were accepted. Other kinds of account have not been seen on a bill line.

rules.message: A GST, TDS or payable account should not be a bill line. Zoho posts GST from the Tax columns and TDS from the TDS columns. Whether Zoho refuses such a line is not known.
rules.fix: Move input GST ledgers to Tax Name, TDS ledgers to the TDS columns.

rules.message: Item Name was empty on every line of our file. Zoho did not complain about it, but those lines failed on other checks first, so it is not yet confirmed that an account-only line is accepted.
rules.fix: Keep Account filled on every line. Confirm with the next test import.

rules.message: An item on a bill must have purchase information.
rules.fix: Import the item as "Sales and Purchases", or leave Item Name empty.

rules.message: Every line needs a Rate.
rules.fix: Write the amount of the line.

rules.message: A line with a negative Rate. Zoho may refuse it: in the first import Zoho added such lines into its total, but those bills failed on another check, so acceptance is not confirmed. A bill whose total is negative is a Vendor Credit, not a bill.
rules.fix: TDS deducted: use TDS Name, TDS Percentage, TDS Amount (and TDS Section Code). Round-off: use Adjustment. A discount: Entity Discount Amount with Discount Account.
rules.evidence_note: 104 of 287 lines were negative in the first import; Zoho summed them into its total (confirmed), acceptance not confirmed.

rules.message: The total of a bill cannot be negative.
rules.fix: Route the voucher to Vendor Credits.

rules.message: When the Total column is in the file, Zoho compares it with the total it works out. An empty Total is read as 0, so every bill is refused ("The given total value 0 and the system generated total value N are not same").
rules.fix: Leave the columns Total, SubTotal, Balance and Item Total out of the file. Zoho works the totals out from Quantity, Rate, tax, TDS, discount and adjustment.
rules.evidence_note: 189 lines refused. Zoho's help says Total is optional and should be unmapped.

rules.message: GST Treatment must be one of Zoho's codes.
rules.fix: Write the same code as on the vendor.

rules.message: GST Treatment is empty. Zoho then takes the treatment of the vendor.
rules.fix: Decide the vendor's treatment in Fix contacts.
rules.evidence_note: First test import: 18 lines had it empty.

rules.message: A registered vendor needs a valid GSTIN on the bill.
rules.fix: Correct it in Fix contacts.

rules.message: Every line of a bill from a GST-registered vendor must carry a tax, an exemption or a reverse charge tax. Zoho refuses it otherwise: "Specify either a Tax or Tax Exemption or Reverse Charge."
rules.fix: The accountant decides per ledger or line what a purchase without GST from a registered vendor is: (1) exempt or nil-rated: write the exemption name in Item Exemption Code (create it first in Tax Exemptions), or the 0% tax GST0 / IGST0; (2) under reverse charge: Reverse Charge Tax Name, Rate and Type; (3) outside GST: see rule BIL-SUPPLY-TYPE-OUT-OF-SCOPE (not yet tried).
rules.evidence_note: 98 lines of 64 bills. Lines of unregistered vendors (business_none) passed this check with no tax.

rules.message: Supply Type "Out of Scope" is in Zoho's bill sample, on a bill of an unregistered vendor. Whether it also satisfies the tax check for a registered vendor has not been tried.
rules.fix: Try it on one bill in the next test import before relying on it.

rules.message: An exemption on a bill of an unregistered vendor is refused ("Tax Exemption should not be applied for GST unRegistered vendors Transaction", reported for the API).
rules.fix: Leave Item Exemption Code empty for business_none vendors.

rules.message: The Item Exemption Code is the name of a tax exemption that exists in Settings > Taxes & Compliance > Taxes > Tax Exemptions. Zoho creates none by default that we know of.
rules.fix: Create the exemptions first (Bulk Create Tax Exemptions) and write the same names.

rules.message: The tax name must exist in Zoho Books.
rules.fix: Use the names from Mapping Studio > Tax mapping.

rules.message: Tax Type is ItemAmount (IGST) or Tax Group (GST).
rules.fix: Write it as in the sample.

rules.message: Tax Name, Tax Type and Tax Percentage go together.
rules.fix: Fill all three or none.

rules.message: The three reverse charge columns go together.
rules.fix: Fill all three or none.

rules.message: A line has a tax, or an exemption, or a reverse charge tax: only one of them.
rules.fix: Keep one.

rules.message: Source and destination in the same state: a GST tax group. Different states: an IGST tax.
rules.fix: Correct the tax or the Source of Supply.

rules.message: The line carries one of Zoho's taxes named for its rate (GST18, IGST5 ...) with another percentage. A Zoho tax has one rate: Zoho Books works the tax out at the rate of the tax named, so the line's tax and the bill total would differ from Tally, or the line is refused.
rules.fix: Write Zoho's tax of the line's rate (leave the Tally ledger unmapped in Mapping Studio, Tax mapping, so each line gets the tax of its own rate) and create the files again.
rules.evidence_note: Audit item GST-001: no import has shown what Zoho does with a tax name whose rate differs from Tax Percentage.

rules.message: IGST cannot be applied as this is an intrastate transaction. A reverse charge tax of IGST needs a Source of Supply in another state (or an overseas vendor); within one state it must be a GST tax group. An empty Source of Supply on a bill of an unregistered vendor counts as the same state.
rules.fix: Use the GST tax group (type Tax Group) for the reverse charge when the supply is within the state, or give the vendor a state in another state / mark it as overseas.
rules.evidence_note: Second test import: 11 bills of two unregistered vendors (Source of Supply empty, reverse charge IGST18) were refused with "IGST cannot be applied as this is an intrastate transaction."

rules.message: Two-letter state codes from Zoho's list.
rules.fix: Use the code from the list.

rules.message: A bill from a registered vendor needs the Source of Supply. If empty Zoho takes the vendor's state.
rules.fix: Write the vendor's state.

rules.message: Destination of Supply is normally the organisation's own state.
rules.fix: Write the organisation's state code.

rules.message: ITC Eligibility: "eligible" is in Zoho's sample. The two "ineligible" codes are assumed from Zoho's screen (Ineligible - As per Section 17(5), Ineligible - Others).
rules.fix: Leave empty (Zoho then treats the tax as eligible) unless input credit is blocked.

rules.message: A bill line of a GST-registered, composition or SEZ vendor carries a 0% tax (GST0 or IGST0) because Tally charged no GST on it. No import has shown yet that Zoho Books takes a 0% tax on such a bill (a composition or SEZ bill may not take a tax at all).
rules.fix: Import one such bill first and look at the result. If Zoho refuses it, write the exemption (Item Exemption Code) instead, or decide the line in Mapping Studio, and create the files again.
rules.evidence_note: Audit item GST-024 (A12): BIL-TAX-REQUIRED-REGISTERED was confirmed only for business_gst lines with no tax; test 2 had no business_gst line with a 0% tax.

rules.message: A bill line of a vendor written as unregistered (GST Treatment business_none or consumer) carries an ordinary GST tax (not under reverse charge), so Zoho Books would book input tax credit from a party with no GSTIN. That credit cannot be claimed under GST (it never appears in GSTR-2B), and no import has shown that Zoho Books takes an ordinary GST tax on such a bill.
rules.fix: Enter the vendor's GSTIN in Fix contacts (the vendor is then registered, business_gst), or, if the vendor really is unregistered, correct the bill in Tally (no GST, or reverse charge) and create the files again. The tool never changes the tax or the amount itself.
rules.evidence_note: Round 1 of the re-check: the three test imports had business_none bill lines with no tax or under reverse charge only. A taxed, non-reverse-charge line of a business_none vendor is not covered, so it is "may be refused".

rules.message: A taxed bill line of a vendor in India with no Source of Supply. Zoho Books then takes the vendor's state; for a vendor with no Place Of Contact it is believed to take the organisation's own state, which would make an inter-state bill (IGST) an intra-state one and refuse or change its tax. Not confirmed by an import.
rules.fix: Give the vendor's state in Tally (or the vendor's GSTIN) and create the files again.
rules.evidence_note: Audit item GST-024 (A12). Test 2 confirmed only IGST0 on overseas invoices with an empty Place of Supply.

params.noneWords: No bill has a TDS Amount that differs from its TDS Percentage of the base by more than a rupee.

rules.message: The TDS Amount of these bills (Tally's, for example under a lower deduction certificate, a threshold crossed or TDS rounded to the rupee) is not the TDS Percentage of the base by more than a rupee. Zoho Books kept the TDS Amount as written where the two agreed; whether it keeps it, works it out again from the percentage, or refuses the bill when they differ has not been seen in an import.
rules.fix: Import one such bill first and compare its TDS with Tally. If Zoho works it out again, set the right percentage in Mapping Studio (TDS mapping) or create a TDS tax of the rate Tally deducted, and create the files again.
rules.evidence_note: Audit item TDS-005: the tests so far had no document with tds_amount_differs.

rules.message: A TDS Name must be a TDS tax in Zoho Books.
rules.fix: Use a name from Settings > Taxes & Compliance > Direct Taxes > Income TDS Rates, or create the tax listed in "TDS taxes to create".
rules.evidence_note: Third test import: every bill and invoice row with a TDS Name was accepted after the TDS taxes were created in Zoho Books with exactly the names, rates and section codes the tool lists ("TDS taxes to create"). The tool cannot see the TDS taxes of the organisation, so these rows stay "may be refused" until the TDS export of Zoho Books is given in the Import Wizard (step "Set up Zoho Books"); with the export every name is checked.

rules.message: A TDS Amount needs its TDS Name.

error_messages.pattern: ^Row already exists\.?$
error_messages.meaning: An account with this name is already in Zoho Books: Zoho created it itself, an earlier import of this same file created it, or someone made it by hand. The row is skipped. No opening balance is lost by that: the tool writes the opening balances in the opening balance journal, not on the rows of this file.
error_messages.fix: Do not rename the ledger and do not type a balance before you have looked. Open the account in Zoho Books. If an earlier import of this file created it, there is nothing to do. If it is one of Zoho's own accounts, leave the row out and use Zoho's account.

error_messages.pattern: ^Opening Balance cannot be associated with the given account\.?$
error_messages.meaning: The row is a Bank account and has an Opening Balance. Zoho does not take a bank opening balance through the Chart of Accounts import. The whole row is refused, so the bank account is not created.
error_messages.fix: Create the files again: the tool writes a Bank, Credit Card or Cash account with Opening Balance and Debit or Credit empty, and its balance is a line of the opening balance journal (OB-1). Import the account again from the retry file. No balance is typed.

error_messages.pattern: ^Invalid row\.?$
error_messages.meaning: Zoho could not read the row. In our imports it was a row whose Account Type does not exist in Zoho Books India ("Long Term Liability"; the India edition calls it "Non Current Liability").
error_messages.fix: Check the Account Type against the list on Accountant > Chart of Accounts > New Account. Use the type from the list, written as listed.

error_messages.pattern: ^Invalid row\.?$
error_messages.meaning: Zoho Books could not use a name on this journal line: the account in the Account column, or the customer or vendor in the Contact Name column, is not in Zoho Books. The whole journal is refused. The other lines of the journal name the column ("This error is related to Row N - Account." or "- Contact Name.").
error_messages.fix: Read the column that the other lines of the journal name. Account: create or import the account first, with exactly the same name. Contact Name: import the missing customer or vendor first. Then import the refused journals again (the retry file).

Account.meaning: On a journal line: the account named in the Account column is not in Zoho Books (in our import: the bank accounts and one other account that the Chart of Accounts import had refused). The whole journal is refused.
Account.fix: Create or import the account first, with exactly the same name, then import the journals again.

Contact Name.meaning: On a journal line: the customer or vendor named in the Contact Name column is not in Zoho Books. The account is not the problem. The whole journal is refused.
Contact Name.fix: Import the missing customer or vendor first (Import Wizard, Customers or Vendors step: upload Zoho's export of its contacts to see which are missing), then import the refused journals again.

error_messages.by_column_note: The follow-on lines of the same journal name the column at fault. The Rejection Manager chooses the cause from that column (zohoerrors.js explainErrorRows). Third test import: one receipt journal was refused with "Invalid row" and "This error is related to Row N - Contact Name." although its accounts existed; the customer on its Accounts Receivable line was not in the organisation (the Customers import had not created it, although the preview showed every row as ready). Journals of the same shape (Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable and a bank line) were accepted in the same import.

error_messages.pattern: ^This error is related to Row (\d+) - (.+?)\.?$
error_messages.meaning: Not an error of its own. The row belongs to the same invoice, bill or journal as row N, and row N has the real error; the text after the dash is the column at fault. Row numbers count the heading row as row 1.
error_messages.fix: Read the message on row N and correct that row. This row needs no change.

error_messages.pattern: ^Duplicate row found in your CSV/TSV file\.?$
error_messages.meaning: The same name is written on two rows of the file. Zoho imports the first and refuses the later one.
error_messages.fix: Merge the two Tally ledgers into one row, or give one of them a different name (and use that name in every voucher file).

error_messages.pattern: ^Enter the selling price of the item\.?$
error_messages.meaning: The Rate column (selling price) is empty on an item that can be sold.
error_messages.fix: Write a selling price in Rate. Zoho needs a number; 0 has not been tried yet.

error_messages.pattern: ^Please ensure that your HSN code has only numbers and length is less than or equal to 8 digits\.?$
error_messages.meaning: Zoho refused the HSN/SAC code. In our import the value was a clean 5-digit number, so the real rule is stricter than the message: 5 digits is not a length Zoho accepts.
error_messages.fix: Write a 4, 6 or 8 digit code. For a service use the 6-digit SAC (it starts with 99). Leave the cell empty if the code is not known.

error_messages.pattern: ^Specify either a Tax or Tax Exemption or Reverse Charge\.?$
error_messages.meaning: The vendor is GST registered (GST Treatment business_gst) and the line has no tax, no exemption and no reverse charge tax.
error_messages.fix: On each such line write one of: a tax (Tax Name, Tax Percentage, Tax Type), an exemption (Item Exemption Code), or a reverse charge tax (Reverse Charge Tax Name, Rate and Type).

error_messages.pattern: ^The given total value ([\d.,-]+) and the system generated total value ([\d.,-]+) are not same\.?$
error_messages.meaning: The Total column was in the file but empty, so Zoho read it as 0 and compared it with the total it worked out itself.
error_messages.fix: Leave the Total, SubTotal, Balance and Item Total columns out of the file (or remove their mapping on the Map Fields page). Zoho works the total out itself.

error_messages.pattern: tax does not exist
error_messages.meaning: The tax named in the file is not in Zoho Books, or the tax type is wrong, or the tax columns were not mapped.
error_messages.fix: Check the name in Settings > Taxes & Compliance > Taxes > Tax Rates. Use the type Tax Group for GST and ItemAmount for IGST (in the Items file: Group and Simple).

error_messages.pattern: specify whether it is tax or not
error_messages.meaning: A line has no tax information.
error_messages.fix: Add the tax name, tax type and tax percentage columns and map them.

error_messages.pattern: IGST must be applied for inter[- ]?state
error_messages.meaning: The place of supply is another state but the line has a GST (CGST+SGST) tax group.
error_messages.fix: Use the IGST tax with type ItemAmount, and check the Place of Supply code.

error_messages.pattern: GST must be applied for int(ra|er)[- ]?state
error_messages.meaning: The place of supply is the organisation's own state but the line has an IGST tax.
error_messages.fix: Use the GST tax group with type Tax Group.

error_messages.pattern: Resource does not exist
error_messages.meaning: The row names another document (estimate, sales order, purchase order, invoice or bill number) that is not in Zoho Books.
error_messages.fix: Leave the reference column empty, or import the document it names first.

error_messages.pattern: Reference Invoice Type is (not valid|invalid)
error_messages.meaning: The Reference Invoice Type does not fit the GST treatment of the contact.
error_messages.fix: Use the value that fits the contact: see lists.reference_invoice_types.

error_messages.pattern: specify the payment received for the invoice
error_messages.meaning: The payment names an invoice but not the amount applied to it.
error_messages.fix: Add the column Amount Applied to Invoice and map it.

error_messages.pattern: enter a valid customer name
error_messages.meaning: The customer is not in Zoho Books under exactly this name.
error_messages.fix: Import the customer first; write the name exactly as in Zoho Books.

error_messages.pattern: mandatory column is missing
error_messages.meaning: A field Zoho requires is not mapped to a column.
error_messages.fix: On the Map Fields page map every field marked with a red asterisk.

error_messages.pattern: value for (the|your) account is incorrect
error_messages.meaning: The account name does not match an account in Zoho Books exactly (spelling, spaces, capital letters).
error_messages.fix: Write the name exactly as in Accountant > Chart of Accounts.

error_messages.pattern: invalid value.*product type
error_messages.meaning: Product Type must be goods or service, in small letters.
error_messages.fix: Write goods or service.

error_messages.pattern: items with only sales information cannot be added
error_messages.meaning: The item on a purchase line has no purchase information.
error_messages.fix: Import the item with Item Type "Sales and Purchases" (with Purchase Rate and Purchase Account), or leave Item Name empty and use the Account.

error_messages.pattern: stock account type cannot be changed
error_messages.meaning: An inventory item was imported again with a different Inventory Account.
error_messages.fix: Write the Inventory Account the item already has.

error_messages.pattern: credit (opening )?balance cannot be imported
error_messages.meaning: A customer with a credit (advance) balance cannot be brought in as an opening balance.
error_messages.fix: Enter the total in Unearned Revenue (Opening Balances) and record a Customer Advance dated before the opening balance date, then Sync.

error_messages.pattern: import (is )?already in progress
error_messages.meaning: Another import has not finished.
error_messages.fix: Wait for the e-mail or notification that the earlier import is complete.

error_messages.pattern: more than 151 columns
error_messages.meaning: The file has more than 151 columns.
error_messages.fix: Remove columns that are not needed.

error_messages.pattern: empty column headers?
error_messages.meaning: The last column of the file has no heading.
error_messages.fix: Remove the empty column (no comma after the last heading).

error_messages.pattern: Tax Exemption should not be applied for GST un[Rr]egistered vendors
error_messages.meaning: An exemption was written on a bill of an unregistered vendor (seen through the API, error code 71510).
error_messages.fix: Leave Item Exemption Code empty when GST Treatment is business_none.

error_messages.pattern: Either Tax or Tax Exemption Reason is required
error_messages.meaning: An invoice line has neither a tax nor an exemption reason (reported for another edition of Zoho Books).
error_messages.fix: Write a tax, or an exemption reason that exists in Zoho Books.

error_messages.pattern: ^Enter the required TDS details\.?$
error_messages.meaning: A row has a TDS Name and a TDS Amount, but TDS Percentage or TDS Section Code is empty. Zoho does not take them from the TDS tax of that name.
error_messages.fix: Write the TDS Percentage and the TDS Section Code on every row that has a TDS Name (the tool does this; create the files again).

error_messages.pattern: IGST cannot be applied as this is an intrastate transaction
error_messages.meaning: A line carries IGST (as the tax or as the reverse charge tax) but Zoho reads the supply as inside one state. With an empty Source of Supply on an unregistered vendor Zoho takes the supply as inside the state.
error_messages.fix: Use the GST tax group for a supply inside the state. For an import of services mark the vendor as overseas. The tool chooses the tax from the two states; check the vendor's state in Fix contacts.

error_messages.pattern: ^Please ensure that the length of the HSN code is a minimum of 6 digits and it has only numbers\.?$
error_messages.meaning: The HSN/SAC field is switched on in Zoho Books and the line has no HSN/SAC or one shorter than 6 digits.
error_messages.fix: Give the income ledger or service item an HSN/SAC code of 6 digits or more (Mapping Studio, HSN/SAC), or switch the field off in Zoho Books (Settings, Setup and Configurations, Items).

opening_balance_route.note: Where the opening balance of a Tally ledger that is not a customer or vendor is written. Every such balance goes into the dated opening balance journal (OB-1), so it does not depend on the Opening Balance Date of the organisation. stays_in_chart_types: types whose balance belongs elsewhere (Accounts Receivable / Payable: the contacts); their balance stays out of the journal. A Stock account is no longer one of them (round 2): a stock balance in the chart may lock the Opening Balance Date before the step "Save the Migration Date" (COA-STOCK-OB-LOCKS-DATE), so it goes into the dated journal OB-3 (an unproven kind of line, its own balancing line) and is listed under Assumptions; if Zoho refuses that line, the balance is typed on Settings > Opening Balances after the Migration Date is saved. date_anchor_type_preference: when a Customers or Vendors file carries opening balances, ONE chart balance stays in the Chart of Accounts file, so that the chart import creates the opening balance record whose date is then edited (Zoho does not save the date while every balance is 0, and nothing may be typed). It is taken from the first type of this list that has a ledger with a balance; these types carried an Opening Balance in our imports or are plain balance sheet types. bank_like_types: accounts Zoho keeps in Banking; never the date anchor.
opening_balance_route.evidence: Equity, Fixed Asset and Other Current Liability rows with an Opening Balance were imported (first and second import). The journal OB-1 was accepted in the second and third import with lines on Zoho's own accounts and bank accounts.

journal_lines_confirmed.note: OB-007: the kinds of opening balance journal line Zoho Books accepted in our test imports. Until a fresh-organisation test proves the other kinds (Retained Earnings, GST system accounts, Credit Card, Cash, Other Asset, Non Current Liability, Stock, Fixed Asset ...), the lines of an unproven kind are written in a journal of their own (OB-3), balanced on Opening Balance Adjustments like OB-1, so that one refused line cannot refuse every opening balance. Journal numbers stay numeric (OB-1, OB-2, OB-3): a letter in the suffix is not documented by Zoho.
journal_lines_confirmed.evidence: docs/ZOHO_IMPORT_RULES.md (Opening balances in the dated journal): OB-1 accepted in the second and third import with lines on bank accounts and on GST Payable, Advance Tax and TDS Receivable. Every other kind: assumed (not yet imported).

second_import_lessons.note: What the second test import (real-data/zoho-test-2) showed. Every item is evidence "Confirmed by second import". No party name, GSTIN or amount of the test data is kept here. The rules that carry each lesson are named, so a change to one can be traced to the other.

entries.lesson: The account type "Long Term Liability" is refused by Zoho Books India with "Invalid row". The type that exists is "Non Current Liability". Loan groups are written with it. No account is made by hand first.

A bill or invoice row with a TDS Name must also have TDS Percentage and TDS Section Code. Zoho Books refuses the row with "Enter the required TDS details." when any of the three is empty. The old advice to leave the section code empty was wrong.

Reverse charge IGST on a supply that Zoho Books reads as inside one state is refused with "IGST cannot be applied as this is an intrastate transaction". An unregistered vendor with an empty Source of Supply is read as inside the home state.
While "Enable the HSN Code or SAC field" is on (the default in a new India organisation), an invoice line with an empty HSN/SAC, or a code that is not at least 6 digits, is refused.

The customers heading is "Place Of Contact" (capital O). Zoho Books did not map the sample's first-row spelling (a small letter o in the word of) by itself on the Map Fields page; its own field list uses the capital.

Zoho Books will not save the Opening Balance (Migration) Date on its own: it asks for at least one balance first. The journal dated the day before the financial year was accepted without the date being saved, and the opening balances of customers and vendors then fell outside the year in the trial balance. The wizard therefore has a step that saves the date together with one real balance, before Customers and Vendors.

A new TDS tax asks for the Applicable Income Tax Act first. For transactions before 01/04/2026 the Old Income Tax Act 1961 is used, with a start date on or before the first day of the financial year. A tax that shows Expired can still be used for past dates.

Zoho Books already has a TDS tax called Commission or Brokerage (its own rate and section). A new tax with the same name and another rate gets the TDS details refused or read wrongly, so the tool gives such a tax a unique name.

Bills of an unregistered vendor with no state were read by Zoho Books as inside the home state. Reverse charge on them must use the GST group (inside the state), unless the vendor is overseas or the state is known and different.
